query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix, whose overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation behavior across different temperatures remain unclear, what single intervention could improve its wear resistance under sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths? State one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains the mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to the unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions, defines the operating limits of the prediction, cites supporting evidence from the introduction, and proposes a falsification experiment capable of resolving microscopic deformation during wear.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a small amount of boron to the FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating can improve its wear resistance under sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of boron
generation.conditions: Sliding conditions spanning different temperatures, friction velocities, and wear depths
generation.mechanism: The boron-rich phase acts as a solid lubricant, reducing friction and wear
generation.baseline: Unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coating tested under identical conditions
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 20-500°C, friction velocity range: 0.1-10 m/s, wear depth range: 0.1-10 mm
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of boron to be added and the optimal processing conditions are uncertain
generation.falsification_experiment: A wear test of the boron-modified FeNiCrCoCu coating against a steel counterbody at 300°C, 5 m/s, and 5 mm wear depth, with microscopic examination of the worn surface

cited_evidence.text: The present work discovers the unique deformation behavior of a refractory high-entropy alloy at elevated temperatures.

args.query: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a Cu matrix wear resistance and microscopic deformation behavior
